key_dates.statement: The gateway page, last updated 30 September 2026, says the application period started on 30 September 2026 and will close on 28 February 2027. The what-you-need-to-do page says the period is open across those dates. PS26/18 uses the same dates for firms wanting to use the transitional arrangements. The 30 June 2026 overview says the window is scheduled to open and close on those dates for the savings provisions.

The what-you-need-to-do page says the regime starts on 25 October 2027, when the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026 take effect. The regime landing page says the regime is expected to come into force on that date. PS26/18 says the Regulations will introduce the new activities from that date. This checker pins the date and does not choose between starts and expected.
The gateway page, the 30 June 2026 overview, and PS26/18 each say that existing registrations do not convert automatically into FSMA permission.
The Travel Rule statement says that from 1 September 2023 UK cryptoasset businesses will be required to collect, verify and share information about cryptoasset transfers.
The marketing page says cryptoasset firms marketing to UK consumers need to comply with the financial promotions regime from 8 October 2023.

sources_and_currency.title: Overview of our cryptoassets regime policy statements
sources_and_currency.notes: Published and last updated 30 June 2026. Names PS26/9 to PS26/13, FG26/5, FG26/6, FG26/7, GC26/4 and GC26/5, and the sourcebooks CRYPTO 2 to CRYPTO 10, CASS 7, CASS 16, CASS 17, COREPRU and CRYPTOPRU. Those PDFs and the Handbook were not opened. The page says the full scope of regulated activities expands from 25 October 2027, that existing registrations will not convert automatically, and that the application window is scheduled to open on 30 September 2026 and close on 28 February 2027 for firms that wish to rely on the savings provisions. The later gateway page is more specific about saving and transitional provisions.

sources_and_currency.title: Cryptoassets: what we expect to see in an application for registration
sources_and_currency.notes: First published 22 March 2023, last updated 30 June 2026. States that the new regime starts on 25 October 2027. Describes BWRA, CRA, CDD, on-chain and off-chain monitoring rules and thresholds, Travel Rule procedures and a flow of funds, a financial promotions policy, and the MLRO. Says registering under the MLRs does not of itself subject the firm to SM&CR. Regulation numbers below are the numbers this page uses. This checker does not interpret the MLRs.

sources_and_currency.title: Cryptoassets: how the gateway will operate
sources_and_currency.notes: Last updated 30 September 2026. Says the application period started on 30 September 2026 and will close on 28 February 2027, as set out in the FCA's direction. Says MLR registration will not convert automatically. Distinguishes firms that apply during the period (saving provision if the application is not determined by commencement), firms that apply outside the period but before commencement (transitional provision: pre-existing contracts only, no new UK contracts), and firms that do not apply (run off before commencement, no saving or transitional provision). The s.21 approvers page named here was not opened.

sources_and_currency.title: What you need to do when preparing for the new cryptoasset regulatory regime
sources_and_currency.notes: Last updated 16 September 2026. Says the application period is open from 30 September 2026 to 28 February 2027, and that the regime starts on 25 October 2027 when the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026 take effect. Encourages firms to carry out a gap analysis. That sentence is the FCA's, not a claim that this tool performs it.

sources_and_currency.title: A new regime for cryptoasset regulation
sources_and_currency.notes: Last updated 30 September 2026. Says the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Cryptoassets) Regulations 2026 were made on 4 February 2026, and that the new regime is expected to come into force on 25 October 2027. The word expected is the landing page's. The what-you-need-to-do page says starts.

sources_and_currency.title: PS26/18: Cryptoasset perimeter guidance
sources_and_currency.notes: Policy statement page published 16 September 2026. The PDF was not opened. The page says that from 25 October 2027 the Cryptoassets Regulations introduce new regulated activities, that existing registrations and permissions will not convert automatically, and that the application window opens on 30 September 2026 and closes on 28 February 2027 for firms wanting to use the transitional arrangements. It also says the FCA plans to consult on further perimeter guidance in late 2026.

sources_and_currency.title: FCA sets out expectations for UK cryptoasset businesses complying with the Travel Rule
sources_and_currency.notes: First published 17 August 2023, last updated 6 February 2026. Says that from 1 September 2023 UK cryptoasset businesses will be required to collect, verify and share information about cryptoasset transfers. Cites Part 7A of the MLRs. Says firms remain responsible when using third-party suppliers, and sets expectations for jurisdictions where the Travel Rule is not in force. JMLSG guidance is mentioned and is not an FCA page, so it is not a source in this catalogue.

sources_and_currency.title: Cryptoasset firms marketing to UK consumers
sources_and_currency.notes: Last updated 6 February 2026. Says the financial promotions regime applies from 8 October 2023, lists four communication routes, and says promotions must be fair, clear and not misleading, with risk warnings and a 24-hour cooling-off period. Names PS23/6 and FG23/3. Those documents were not opened. The page still describes GC23/2 as a guidance consultation and still says legislation on a promotions gateway was before Parliament. This catalogue does not overwrite that sentence.
